long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Sichuan, Wang spent sixteen years in the People's Liberation Army and then worked in Dalian's Xigang district government. In 1988, he took charge of its debt-laden housing developer, using a bank loan and an urban-renewal project to restore the enterprise. That state-company platform and his official networks materially shaped Wanda's beginning.

Wang restructured the business into Dalian Wanda Group and shifted it from housing into commercial complexes anchored by Wanda Plazas. The group later added cinemas, film production, tourism and investment, while property remained the core wealth engine. After an overseas acquisition spree, debt pressure led Wanda to sell hotels, tourism assets, most of its AMC stake and control of a mall-management unit. Wang remains chairman, directing a narrower conglomerate still centred on Chinese commercial real estate.
